extracted.intended_audience: late-night TV comedy writers, stand-up/TV joke writers, and developers of computational humor (Witscript)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for generating and evaluating short topical jokes for late-night television using identifiable formulas, 'handles' from the news, and the Witscript computational pipeline. Focuses on anatomy of a joke, common joke formulas, and a five-question rubric for quality filtering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Premise — identifiable formulas and handles
rubrics_metrics.description: The jokes that got the biggest laughs follow identifiable formulas populated with "handles" — people, places, things — each with a variety of related associations that combine to form a punch line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use familiar 'handles' from the news or audience knowledge; populate a formula with associations related to that handle so the punch line emerges from linked associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witscript — Keyword Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: NLP and word embeddings find the keyword pair most likely to seed a joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select keyword pairs (handles/terms) with high associative potential as the initial seed for joke generation; these drive subsequent association linking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witscript — Association Linking
rubrics_metrics.description: Word associations with the best wordplay link to create a punch line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate associations between the seed keywords that enable wordplay or unexpected connections; prioritize links that lead to a clear punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witscript — Bridge Text Generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine-tuned language model fills the gap between input and punch line in a natural-sounding way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate natural-sounding bridge text that connects topic/angle to the punch without telegraphing it; the bridge should read plausibly as part of a host's line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witscript — Quality Filtering
rubrics_metrics.description: Only outputs jokes that exceed a preset score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply scoring/thresholds to filter generated jokes; retain only those meeting preset quality metrics (e.g., novelty, coherence, punch effectiveness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomy — Topic (familiar news handle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic → familiar news handle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a handle the audience will recognize (person/place/thing from recent news); the joke should be anchored to that specific handle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomy — Angle (secondary aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Angle → secondary aspect
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a specific, often less-obvious aspect or perspective on the handle to serve as the angle that will connect to the punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomy — Punch line (connects topic and angle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Punch line → connects topic and angle via wordplay or unexpected association
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The punch should link the topic and angle by exploiting wordplay or a shared/contrasting association; clarity of the link is essential for the laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomy — Tag (optional escalation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag → optional second punchline that escalates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a tag to escalate or extend the laugh after the main punch, but only if it adds value and remains specific to the handle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Formula — The Comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comparison (X is like Y because Z)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure jokes by likening the handle to something else and explain the likeness with a punchy reason (Z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Formula — The Reverse
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reverse (turn the obvious meaning around)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take an expected interpretation of the handle or statement and invert it to create surprise; flip assumptions to reveal humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Formula — The Pun
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pun
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit multiple meanings, homophones, or wordplay on the handle or angle to produce a punch; ensure punch is clear and not forced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Formula — The Misdirection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Misdirection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead the audience down one interpretive path and then reveal an unexpected conclusion; the set-up should plausibly support the redirection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Formula — The Personification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Personification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute human traits, motives, or dialogue to non-human handles (places, objects, institutions) to create humorous contrast or commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Formula — The Fake-Out Quote
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fake-Out Quote
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a line that sounds like a real quote or statement, then subvert expectations with an invented or absurd finish that becomes the punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Formula — The Topical Mash-Up
rubrics_metrics.description: The Topical Mash-Up
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine two current handles/topics in an unexpected way so associations from both collide to produce humor; ideal for rapidly topical jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric Item 1 — recognizable handle from news/audience knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a recognizable handle from the news/audience knowledge?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify the joke centers on a handle the audience will know; without recognition, the associations and punch lose impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric Item 2 — specific angle on the handle
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the angle on the handle specific?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the joke targets a specific aspect of the handle rather than making a generic observation; specificity increases punch clarity and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric Item 3 — punch links via wordplay or shared association
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the punch line link via wordplay or shared association?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the punch arises from a clear link—wordplay or shared/crosstalk association—between topic and angle rather than vague irony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric Item 4 — natural bridge between topic and punch
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the bridge between topic and punch natural?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the transitional wording feels like a natural utterance and does not awkwardly telegraph the joke; the bridge should make the punch feel earned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric Item 5 — joke specificity to the handle (not generic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the joke specifically about the handle, not generic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the joke's content and references are tied to the handle; jokes that could apply to any subject are weaker for topical late-night delivery.
